# s249 — refs must let slice text mark a reference as an example

`slicer refs` checks every `path:line` it finds. Slice text that quotes example references, for instance a spec for `refs` itself, therefore always reports `missing_file`, and `refs` can never exit 0 for that item. There needs to be a way to say "this is an example, not a reference".

**Findings:** first slicer refs run on main, 2026-10-11: 6 of 7 reports were s248's example refs; no way to silence them · **Size:** S · **Trees:** src/slicer, tests, docs

**2026-10-11** — Ready for review: refs skips examples. Lines inside fenced code blocks (backtick or tilde, up to 3 spaces in, closer with no trailing text) and lines containing <!-- example --> are not checked; line numbers and offsets still count them. 8 new find() tests, mutation-checked; full suite 1623 OK; relay gate VERDICT: PASS. Owner decision: s248's lead examples stay unmarked until s252 (edit --lead) lands, so refs still reports those two; s248's Why examples are marked.

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:** the shared-line anchor rule (s248); config-level ignore lists; changing which text refs scans.

## Why

On 2026-10-11, the first run of `slicer refs` on main after s246 landed reported 7 problems. 6 of them came from the example lines in s248's own spec (`src/app.py:1`, `a.py:5`, ...), and nothing could silence them. If an example counts as drift, `refs` becomes noise exactly in the specs that describe it. <!-- example -->

**Decision (owner, final): option (c), both rules apply.**

1. References inside fenced code blocks are skipped. Fences open with ``` or ~~~ (optionally indented up to 3 spaces). A fence closes on a line of the same character, at least as long as the opener, with nothing after it but spaces or tabs, up to 3 spaces in. A backtick opener's info string may not contain a backtick.
2. Every reference on a line that contains the HTML comment `<!-- example -->` is skipped.
